body.question: Does the inventory cover the front room or the whole building?
body.why_now: The room schedule depends on how much counting you intended.

options.label: Front room only
options.consequence: One volunteer can count the trays before lunch.

options.label: Whole building
options.consequence: The team includes the storage room during the afternoon shift.

body.level_reason: The coordinator chooses how the work should proceed.

body.question: Does rotate the display mean turn the stand or exchange the books?
body.why_now: The two readings change what visitors see.

options.label: Turn the stand
options.consequence: The current books face the doorway.

options.label: Exchange the books
options.consequence: Visitors see a different selection on the same stand.

body.level_reason: The coordinator chooses how the work should proceed.

body.question: Did you authorize sharing the lending guide with visitors?
body.why_now: A volunteer relayed permission. The coordinator can confirm the intended release.

options.label: Release both sections
options.consequence: Visitors can take the main guide and its appendix.

options.label: Release the guide alone
options.consequence: Visitors receive the main guide while the appendix stays at the desk.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.consequence: Staff keep using the existing arrangement for this session.

evidence.claim: The desk copy contains a main guide and a separate appendix.

body.question: May we make the planting diagrams public in the visitor booklet?
body.why_now: The booklet goes to print before the spring opening.

options.label: Publish all diagrams
options.consequence: Readers may keep and share every planting diagram in the booklet.

options.label: Publish one diagram
options.consequence: Only the entrance layout becomes public.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.consequence: Staff keep using the existing arrangement for this session.

evidence.claim: The proof contains six planting diagrams.

body.question: May staff clear last season's duplicate packs?
body.why_now: The packing bench needs shelf space.

options.label: Clear all duplicates
options.consequence: Staff remove thirty packets weighing two kilograms.

options.label: Clear the empty packets
options.consequence: Staff discard eight empty packets and retain the filled ones.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.consequence: Staff keep using the existing arrangement for this session.

evidence.claim: A trial count found thirty duplicates, including eight empty packets, weighing two kilograms in total.

body.question: May the desk replace the room signs?
body.why_now: The coordinator controls changes to printed directions.

options.label: Replace all room signs
options.consequence: Every doorway uses the new visitor directions.

options.label: Replace the entrance sign
options.consequence: Only the directions at the entrance change.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.consequence: Staff keep using the existing arrangement for this session.

evidence.claim: Four doorways have replaceable sign holders.

body.question: By the return box, did you mean the wooden chest or the wire basket?
body.why_now: The move list mentions a return box without a material or location.

options.label: Wooden chest
options.consequence: Staff move the chest from the reading room.

options.label: Wire basket
options.consequence: Staff move the basket beside the stairs.

body.level_reason: The coordinator chooses how the work should proceed.

evidence.claim: The chest may be the intended box because it has a return label.

body.question: Should the desk accept the new counting sheet as a source for its weekly total?
body.why_now: The next weekly report needs a source for walk-in counts.

options.label: Accept the sheet
options.consequence: The total includes the new desk counts.

options.label: Keep the old sources
options.consequence: Walk-in counts stay separate for this issue.

body.level_reason: The coordinator chooses how the work should proceed.

body.question: Can you prepare a sample ticket with identifying marks covered?
body.why_now: The print crew needs a sample it can show at a public workshop.

steps.command: Cover the identifying boxes and copy one ticket.
steps.expected_result: The copy shows the ticket layout and blank identifying boxes.
steps.why_person: Only the desk coordinator can handle the original ticket.

body.level_reason: Only the person at the workshop can make this observation.

body.question: Can you clear the expired reservation on the proof rack?
body.why_now: The printer is waiting for a rack that still displays yesterday's reservation.

steps.command: Check that the dated reservation has ended, then turn its marker to Available.
steps.expected_result: The rack shows Available and can receive today's proof.
steps.why_person: A person at the desk must check the physical reservation tag.

body.level_reason: Only the person at the workshop can make this observation.

body.question: How should the main workbench receive the new assembly instructions?
body.why_now: The workbench has local notes that staff still use.

options.label: Replace the instruction set
options.consequence: The main bench uses the complete new edition after its notes are saved.

options.label: Transfer the changed pages
options.consequence: Staff keep their local notes and replace the two revised pages.

body.level_reason: The coordinator chooses how the work should proceed.

body.question: How should the second workshop get the new booking slips?
body.why_now: Its binder has local inserts and the new slips must reach it before opening.

options.label: Exchange the binder
options.consequence: The second workshop starts with a fresh copy and files the local inserts separately.

options.label: Send the slips alone
options.consequence: The second workshop clips the new slips into its current binder.

body.level_reason: The coordinator chooses how the work should proceed.
